# SBE golden fixtures

Sixty-two messages, encoded by the **reference's own** `sbe-tool` output, with
the **reference's own** decoder's reading of each one recorded beside it. Both
sides of the comparison therefore come from the same program the reference's
Java codecs come from, which is what makes a disagreement with `deepmsg-codec`
this repository's defect rather than the tool's opinion (ADR-0004).

| | |
|---|---|
| Schemas | `schemas/aeron-archive-codecs.xml` (101/14), `schemas/aeron-archive-mark-codecs.xml` (100/2) |
| Fixtures | 61 from schema 101, 1 from schema 100 |
| Readings | 680 |
| Generated by | `Generate.java`, from `aeron-all-1.53.2.jar` |
| Captured | 2026-10-05 |

## The files

`NNN-TTT-<name>.bin` — one message each, message header included: schema id,
template id, then the message name, both zero-padded so the directory sorts the
way the schemas do. The bytes are exactly what
`io.aeron.archive.codecs.<Message>Encoder` wrote, with no edit of any kind.

`golden.tsv` — the reference's reading of each one, and the only place a value
appears. Three kinds of line:

    fixture <name> <file> <schemaId> <templateId> <version> <bytes>
    header  <name> <version> <field> <type> <value>
    field   <name> <version> <field> <type> <value>

Every `header` and `field` line is what `io.aeron.archive.codecs.*Decoder`
*answers* for that file at that acting version — not what the generator put in.
The generator computes nothing about what a value should decode to; that is the
difference between a golden and a hope.

`type` is `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `ascii`, `data` (hex), or
`enum:<Name>` — whose value is `<NAME>:<raw>`, so the name and the wire integer
are both pinned.

## The second version of a few fixtures

A handful of messages have fields added after the message was introduced
(`sinceVersion`). For those, `golden.tsv` carries a second set of readings at
the version just below the first such field, where the decoder has to answer
with a null instead of the bytes physically present:

| Fixture | Second reading | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `control-response-*` | 3 | `version` answers its null `0` |
| `replay-request`, `bounded-replay-request`, `replicate-request-2` | 6 | `fileIoMaxLength`, `replayToken` answer `i32`/`i64` null |
| `auth-connect-request` | 11 | `clientInfo` answers empty |
| `mark-file-header` | 1 and 0 | `headerLength`/`errorBufferLength`, then `archiveId` (`-1`) |

These are **readings, not fixtures**, because no such message can be *encoded*.
`sbe-tool`'s Java encoder has no version guard at all — it writes every field
whatever the header says, which a probe against the jar confirmed — so the only
old version the reference can be asked about is the one it reads. The generator
lowers the header's `version` byte in a copy and asks the reference decoder for
its answer; the committed `.bin` keeps the version the encoder wrote.

## Regenerating

The generator needs the reference's `aeron-all` fat jar, which is a build
product of the sibling checkout rather than a published artifact:

    cd ../aeron && ./gradlew :aeron-all:jar      # if it is not already built
    ls aeron-all/build/libs/aeron-all-1.53.2.jar

Then, from this repository's root:

    java --add-exports java.base/jdk.internal.misc=ALL-UNNAMED \
         -cp ../aeron/aeron-all/build/libs/aeron-all-1.53.2.jar \
         tests/fixtures/sbe/Generate.java

The `--add-exports` is agrona's, not ours: it reaches for
`jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe`, which the module system stopped handing out in Java
17. The generator refuses to run if the codecs it loaded did not come from a
file named `aeron-all-1.53.2.jar`, because a different build of the same classes
is a different encoder and the golden would blame `deepmsg-codec` for it.

Two runs are byte-identical — the value rule draws on the field names and the
schema, and on nothing else — so `git status` after a re-run is the determinism
check. A `.bin` no message produces any more stops the run before anything is
written, rather than being left behind as a fixture that passes because nobody
looks at it.

## What is covered, and what is not

Covered: every field of every message in both schemas, its offset and width;
both variable-length encodings (36 of them — 28 `varAscii` and 4 `varData` in
schema 101, 4 `varAscii` in schema 100); the message header's four fields;
the mark file header's declared 128-byte block with its explicit `offset=`
fields; the version-gated fields above; and every valid value of all five enums
— `ControlResponseCode`, `SourceLocation`, `BooleanType`, `RecordingState`,
`RecordingSignal` — which is why three messages appear once per variant rather
than once.

Not covered, deliberately:

- **Repeating groups.** Neither schema has one, so there is no group encoding to
  pin.
- **The cluster schemas** (111, 110, 112). They are carried in `schemas/` for
  the cluster track and nothing depends on their contents yet
  (`schemas/README.md`); their fixtures belong to that track.
- **A message encoded at an old acting version.** `sbe-tool` cannot produce
  one; see above.
